record.original_question: Does there exist an integer D such that every 2-degenerate graph G with Delta(G) > D satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5 Delta(G) / 2? More generally, does there exist an integer D such that every graph G with Delta(G) > D and maximum average degree mad(G) < 4 also satisfies chi(G^2) <= 5 Delta(G) / 2?

evidence.quote: Question 24 ([96]). Is there an integer D such that every graph G with ∆(G) > D that is 2-degenerate satisfies χ2(G) 6 5∆(G)/2?
Question 25 ([96]). Is there an integer D such that every graph G with ∆(G) > D and mad(G) < 4 satisfies χ2(G) 6 5∆(G)/2?

There exists an integer D such that every graph G with ∆(G) > D that is 2-degenerate satisfies χ2(G) 6 5∆(G)/2. More generally, there exists an integer D such that every graph G with ∆(G) > D and mad(G) < 4 satisfies χ2(G) 6 5∆(G)/2. These are Questions 24 and 25. They are both best possible due to the construction in Theorem 23.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple graph $G$, let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree and let $G^2$ denote the square of $G$, i.e., the graph on the same vertex set in which two distinct vertices are adjacent whenever their distance in $G$ is at most $2$. Let $\chi(G^2)$ be the chromatic number of $G^2$. Recall that $G$ is $2$-degenerate if every subgraph of $G$ contains a vertex of degree at most $2$, and the maximum average degree of $G$ is $\mathrm{mad}(G) = \max\{2|E(H)|/|V(H)| : H \subseteq G,\, V(H) \neq \emptyset\}$.

(a) Does there exist an integer $D$ such that every $2$-degenerate graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) > D$ satisfies
$$\chi(G^2) \le \tfrac{5\,\Delta(G)}{2}\,?$$

(b) More generally, does there exist an integer $D$ such that every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) > D$ and $\mathrm{mad}(G) < 4$ satisfies
$$\chi(G^2) \le \tfrac{5\,\Delta(G)}{2}\,?$$
artifact.category_tag: Graph coloring / squares of sparse graphs
artifact.status_search_result: The questions are stated as open in surveys on coloring squares of sparse graphs, and a web search did not locate a published resolution. The bound $5\Delta/2$ is known to be best possible (matching constructions exist) but no proof of the upper bound for large $\Delta$ on $2$-degenerate graphs or graphs with $\mathrm{mad}(G)<4$ was found.

status_evidence.title: Improved square coloring of planar graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bounds on chromatic number of squares of sparse/planar graphs, leaving the 5Δ/2 question for 2-degenerate and mad<4 graphs unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Open status of the 5Δ/2 bound for squares of 2-degenerate / mad<4 graphs is referenced in the literature on square coloring.
